titleEn: Asking for a quieter hotel room
titleTh: ขอเปลี่ยนห้องพักที่เงียบกว่า
scenarioSentences: You are staying at a hotel for three nights.
Your room is next to the elevator.
It is noisy all night.
Mr. Hughes works at reception.
You go down to see him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good morning. Could I change rooms, please? Mine is very noisy.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hughes
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. What's the problem?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's right next to the elevator. I heard it all night.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hughes
dialogue.text: That room is often noisy. Let me check what's free.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'm here for two more nights.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hughes
dialogue.text: I have a quiet room on the eighth floor, away from the elevator.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds much better. Is it the same price?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hughes
dialogue.text: Yes, it is. You can move after eleven o'clock today.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. Should I leave my old key here?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hughes
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I'll give you the new one now.

titleTh: ขายโทรศัพท์มือถือเครื่องเก่า
scenarioSentences: You are selling your old phone online.
Ali is interested in buying it.
The phone has a small scratch.
Ali calls you with questions.
You hope to sell it this week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Ali. Thanks for calling about the phone.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.text: Hi. Is it still for sale? And does it work well?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, it works perfectly. The battery lasts all day.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.text: Great. Are there any problems with it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: There's a small scratch on the back, but the screen is perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.text: Hmm. Would you take one hundred seventy dollars, then?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How about one hundred eighty? I'll include the case and charger.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.text: Okay, that's fair. Where can we meet?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm on campus every day. Could we meet outside the library at noon?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.text: Sure, tomorrow at noon. I'll bring cash.

titleEn: Changing a restaurant booking for more people
titleTh: เพิ่มจำนวนคนในการจองร้านอาหาร
scenarioSentences: You booked a table for four people.
Now eight friends want to come.
Ms. Dubois manages the restaurant.
You call her on Friday.
You hope she can help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Dubois. I booked a table for four at seven on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Dubois
dialogue.text: Yes, I see it. How can I help?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could we change it to eight people? More friends want to come.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Dubois
dialogue.text: Our tables for eight are full at seven.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Oh no. Is there another time that might work?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Dubois
dialogue.text: I have a big table by the window at eight o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's a bit late, but fine. Do we need to order early?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Dubois
dialogue.text: No, but there's a small service charge for big groups.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's okay. Please change it to eight people at eight.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Dubois
dialogue.text: Done. See you on Saturday.

titleEn: Starting a running routine with a friend
titleTh: เริ่มวิ่งออกกำลังกายกับเพื่อน
scenarioSentences: You want to get fitter.
You have never run regularly before.
Your friend Jade runs every week.
She offers to run with you.
You meet for coffee to plan.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Jade, thanks for offering to run with me.

dialogue.speaker: Jade
dialogue.text: No problem! How often can you run?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Maybe three times a week. Mornings are best for me.

dialogue.speaker: Jade
dialogue.text: Mornings suit me too. How about Monday, Wednesday and Friday at seven?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That works. How far should we run at first?

dialogue.speaker: Jade
dialogue.text: Just two kilometers. If you start too far, you might get hurt.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Two sounds easy enough. When can we go further?

dialogue.speaker: Jade
dialogue.text: We'll add a little each week, until you can run five.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. Should I buy new running shoes first?

dialogue.speaker: Jade
dialogue.text: Your old ones are fine for now. See you Monday!

titleTh: เป็นอาสาสมัครที่ศูนย์พักพิงสัตว์
scenarioSentences: You love animals.
You want to do some volunteer work.
There is an animal shelter near your home.
Mr. Ward is the shelter manager.
You visit him to ask about helping.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Mr. Ward. I'd like to volunteer here. How can I help?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ward
dialogue.text: We need people to clean, feed the animals or walk the dogs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd love to walk the dogs. I grew up with dogs.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ward
dialogue.text: Great. How many hours can you give each week?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I have classes on weekdays, but I'm free on Saturday mornings.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ward
dialogue.text: Saturdays are perfect. We walk the dogs from nine to twelve.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's great. Do I need any training first?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ward
dialogue.text: Yes, there's a one-hour lesson this Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sounds good. What should I wear?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ward
dialogue.text: Old clothes and comfortable shoes. The dogs get very excited!

titleEn: Learning to cook on a small budget
titleTh: หัดทำอาหารแบบประหยัด
scenarioSentences: You moved into your own apartment.
You spend too much money on takeout food.
Your friend Inés is a good cook.
She cooks cheap, healthy meals.
You ask her for advice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Inés, can you teach me to cook? I spend too much on takeout.

dialogue.speaker: Inés
dialogue.text: Of course! What do you usually eat?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mostly burgers and pizza. They're expensive and not very healthy.

dialogue.speaker: Inés
dialogue.text: Rice and vegetables are cheaper and healthier. They're a good start.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: But I don't know which vegetables to buy.

dialogue.speaker: Inés
dialogue.text: Buy what's in season at the market. It's cheaper and fresher.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How much should I spend each week?

dialogue.speaker: Inés
dialogue.text: About thirty dollars is enough if you plan your meals.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could we cook together this weekend so I can learn?

dialogue.speaker: Inés
dialogue.text: Sure. Come on Saturday, and we'll make vegetable fried rice.

titleTh: เรียกช่างซ่อมก๊อกน้ำรั่ว
scenarioSentences: Your kitchen tap is leaking.
It drips all night, so you can't sleep.
Mr. Burke is a plumber.
You call him in the evening.
You want it fixed soon.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Mr. Burke. My kitchen tap is leaking. Can you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Burke
dialogue.text: Sure. How bad is the leak?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It drips all the time. I've put a bowl under it.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Burke
dialogue.text: I'm busy tonight, but I can come tomorrow morning at nine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine. But what should I do until then?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Burke
dialogue.text: Turn off the water under the sink. There's a small handle there.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I see it. Should I turn it to the right?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Burke
dialogue.text: Yes, turn it all the way. The dripping should stop.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. How much will the repair cost?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Burke
dialogue.text: Probably about fifty dollars, if I don't need new parts.

titleEn: Finding a quiet place to study
titleTh: หาที่เงียบ ๆ สำหรับอ่านหนังสือ
scenarioSentences: You live in a busy dorm.
Your neighbors are loud every evening.
You have a big exam soon.
Paul is in your history class.
You ask him where he studies.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Paul, where do you study? My dorm is too noisy in the evenings.

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.text: I usually go to the library. They have small study rooms upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Really? I didn't know that. Are they free to use?

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.text: Yes, but you have to book them online first.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How long can you keep a room?

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.text: Two hours at a time. In the evening, they're often empty.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's perfect. I'm usually busy until six anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.text: I'm going at seven tonight. Book the room next to mine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. We could take a coffee break together.

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.text: Sure. I'll send you the booking link now.

titleTh: จัดงานแลกเสื้อผ้ากับเพื่อน
scenarioSentences: Your closet is full of old clothes.
You rarely wear most of them.
Your friend Bella feels the same.
You want to plan a clothes swap.
You talk about it at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Bella, let's organize a clothes swap. We both have too many clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Bella
dialogue.text: Great idea! Just us, or more people?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Our classmates too. Everyone can bring things they don't wear anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Bella
dialogue.text: How many items should each person bring?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Maybe five, so the swap stays fair.

dialogue.speaker: Bella
dialogue.text: Good. We'll need a big space for that.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The student center has a free room on Friday afternoon. I've already asked.

dialogue.speaker: Bella
dialogue.text: Perfect. What should we do with the clothes nobody takes?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We could give them to a charity.

dialogue.speaker: Bella
dialogue.text: Nice. I'll make a poster and share it online tonight.

titleEn: Asking a neighbor about recycling days
titleTh: ถามเพื่อนบ้านเรื่องวันทิ้งขยะรีไซเคิล
scenarioSentences: You just moved into a new house.
You are not sure about the recycling rules.
Mrs. Gray lives next door.
She has lived there for years.
You knock on her door.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Mrs. Gray. I'm your new neighbor. Could I ask about recycling?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Gray
dialogue.text: Of course! Welcome to the street.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Which bin is for plastic? There are three by my door.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Gray
dialogue.text: The yellow one is for plastic, and the blue one is for paper.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And the green one?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Gray
dialogue.text: That's for food waste. It's collected every Monday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: When do they collect plastic and paper?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Gray
dialogue.text: Plastic goes on Tuesday, and paper on Friday. Put the bins out the night before.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. I might forget, so I'll write it on my calendar.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Gray
dialogue.text: Good idea. If you forget, just ask me.
